notes: TBox rule edit: Roman aqueducts moved water by gravity alone; the edit makes them pump it, which is plausible (the Romans knew force pumps) and clearly false. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is stated directly and follows from nothing. No real exceptions: inverted siphons, as at Lyon, still run on the head of water. The three derived queries name aqueducts (the Eifel and Gadara aqueducts, the Pont d'Aël) as Roman aqueducts in the prompt, so the rule is their only route: determinate. The famous members (the Pont du Gard, Segovia) are not asked. The Chinese and Spanish cross-lingual questions are choices (gravity or pumps) with the short gold 重力 / por gravedad. The near query (Vitruvius) differs from the new answer and is no premise. Caveat: the Eifel Aqueduct's gravity flow is stated in its own Wikipedia article (37 of 223 Dolma mentions co-occur with gravity), so a model holding it by name may keep 'gravity'.
